tasks.task: Confirm site readiness and establish site control
tasks.scope: Verify building unoccupied, confirm skip-bin access via loading dock, establish exclusion zones around demolition perimeter, confirm services isolation pre-work checklist complete
hazards: Services still energised — electric shock or arc flash during work setup
Asbestos-containing materials not identified or isolated — inhalation exposure before removal phase
tasks.dominant_hazard: Services still energised — electric shock or arc flash during work setup
controls: Verify all electrical switchboards are isolated, locked off, and tagged with 'DO NOT OPERATE' notices at point of isolation.
Confirm building is unoccupied — conduct walk-through with site supervisor and record occupancy status in site diary.
Confirm skip-bin access via loading dock is clear — measure and photograph access route before skip placement.
Brief all site personnel on exclusion zone boundaries, services status, and asbestos locations before work starts.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any energised electrical circuit is discovered not listed on isolation checklist or tag-lock is disturbed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: building occupant is found on site or unauthorised person enters exclusion zone.
admin: Record building occupancy confirmation in site diary with date, time, and supervisor name.
Verify all workers hold White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and asbestos-related licences (CPCCDE3002 or CPCCDE3014 as applicable) — check before induction.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: before any demolition work commences, then daily at start of shift
monitoring.evidence: Site diary entry recording isolation checklist sign-off, occupancy confirmation, and asbestos survey review completion date and reviewer name

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class B licence
tasks.scope: Licensed asbestos removalist to remove vinyl floor tiles and pipe lagging identified in asbestos survey report; containment, removal, and disposal according to asbestos removal licence and statutory requirements
tasks.hrcw_category: WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.4 — Disturbance of asbestos
hazards: Inhalation of asbestos fibres — exposure during removal, handling, or transport
Contamination of non-removal areas — fibres spread outside containment during work
Inadequate waste containment — asbestos waste exposure during bagging or bin loading
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of asbestos fibres — exposure during removal, handling, or transport
controls: Establish full containment enclosure around removal area — seal doors, windows, penetrations with heavy-duty plastic sheeting and duct tape before any disturbance.
Operate negative pressure unit with HEPA filtration during all removal work — maintain continuous extraction and monitor pressure gauge remains in negative range.
Apply water mist to asbestos materials 15 minutes before removal and keep damp throughout disturbance — use low-pressure spray only, never dry cut or break out.
Place all removed asbestos materials immediately into labelled heavy-duty asbestos waste bags — seal and label each bag with asbestos warning label and licence holder name before any movement.
Decontaminate all waste bags and external containment surfaces with damp cloths before transport from removal area — remove visible dust.
Brief licensed removalist and all workers on removal method, contamination risk zones, and emergency procedures before any work starts.
Monitor air quality during removal using real-time particle counter — record readings every 30 minutes and stop work if airborne fibre level cannot be controlled.
Establish exclusion zone 2 metres beyond containment boundary — prohibit all unauthorised entry and restrict to licensed removalist and safety supervisor only.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start removal until: licensed asbestos removalist and site safety supervisor on site, containment enclosure complete and pressure-tested to negative, water supply confirmed operational, and waste disposal contractor confirmed to receive labelled asbestos waste.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: negative pressure unit fails or containment is breached — seal and do not re-enter until containment is restored and re-tested.
🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression fails or materials become dry during disturbance — re-dampen before continuing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: air monitoring shows fibre level cannot be controlled or respirator fails — evacuate containment, decontaminate, and reassess before re-entry.
admin: tell SafeWork NSW of asbestos removal work according to WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.18 — obtain written acknowledgement.
Complete and retain asbestos removal work method statement including containment design, removal sequence, waste transport route, and disposal contractor details.
Record air monitoring readings on site — retain for 5 years post-removal.
Arrange Class B waste transporter and licensed asbestos waste disposal facility before removal commencement.
Decontaminate site after removal — wipe all non-removal areas and surfaces with damp cloth, dispose of contamination cloths as asbestos waste.
ppe: Type 3 or 4 protective suit with integral hood and booties
Organic vapour and P2 combination respirator (not P2 alone)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: continuous during removal, recorded every 30 minutes
monitoring.evidence: Real-time particle counter readings recorded on site log; negative pressure unit display visible and documented

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove partition walls and structural supports
tasks.scope: Strip and remove all non-load-bearing partition walls, studs, and temporary supports; protect primary structure; manage falling-object exclusion zone for full demolition height plus 5m
hazards: Unintended collapse of primary structure — inadequate support or incorrect member identification
Struck by swinging or shifting wall sections — manual or tool-assisted removal
tasks.dominant_hazard: Falling objects from full demolition height plus 5m exclusion zone — struck by debris or structural member
controls: Install debris containment netting or hoarding to full height plus 2m to capture falling objects and dust within exclusion zone.
Cut and lower wall sections manually or with hand tools; do not drop or swing unsupported sections.
Disconnect or isolate all services within partition walls (electrical, water, gas, HVAC) before removal; tag and verify isolation.
check primary structure for damage, lateral movement, or unintended settlement after each major wall removal; stop work if movement detected.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start partition wall removal until: structural engineer has identified and approved all load-bearing members in writing and confirmed sequence of removal.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: primary structure shows lateral movement, vertical settlement, cracking, or any sign of instability.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached or debris escapes containment netting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unidentified load-bearing member or unexpected structural condition is encountered during removal.
admin: Obtain asbestos removal permit and Class A or B licence before work starts.
Appoint structural engineer to oversee member identification and sequence approval.
Conduct air monitoring during any friable asbestos removal (Class A); record results daily.
ppe: High-visibility vest (all personnel in or near exclusion zone).
Organic vapour respirator or P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) where dust suppression is marginal (SDS Section 8 and site assessment).
Eye protection (impact-rated glasses for cutting and debris removal).

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.who: Structural engineer (approval); Site supervisor (daily verification); Workers (pre-removal briefing).
monitoring.frequency: Structural engineer: before removal sequence approval and after major removal milestones. Supervisor: before each shift and after each large wall removal. Air monitoring: continuous during friable asbestos removal.
monitoring.evidence: Engineer sign-off on member identification drawing; supervisor daily log of exclusion zone integrity and structure condition checks; air monitoring certificates (if Class A); photographic record of containment integrity.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove partition walls and structural
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove partition walls and structural per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove floor coverings and adhesive backing
tasks.scope: Strip vinyl tiles, carpet, and adhesive remnants from concrete floor slab; include perimeter skirting and trims; contain dust and manage waste for appropriate disposal
hazards: Dust inhalation — silica or vinyl dust released during stripping and adhesive removal
Chemical exposure — adhesive fumes or solvents during wet removal or grinding
Cut or puncture wound — sharp tools or concealed fasteners during stripping work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Dust inhalation — silica or vinyl dust released during stripping and adhesive removal
controls: Establish wet suppression protocol: spray floor with water mist before and during scraping to prevent dust release; maintain damp surface throughout stripping work.
Install local exhaust ventilation or portable dust extractor with HEPA filter at point of removal; maintain continuous extraction during scraping and grinding operations.
Wear organic vapour respirator (per SDS Section 8) when adhesive fumes present; switch to P2 particulate mask if only dust generation observed and wet suppression fails.
Barricade work area with plastic sheeting and tape seams; restrict access to licensed floor stripping personnel only; maintain negative air pressure if available.
Check floor substrate before stripping for concealed fasteners, wire mesh, or unknown materials; stop work immediately if asbestos-containing material is suspected.
Use hand tools (floor scraper, putty knife) in preference to power grinders where practicable; if grinding required, operate within dust extraction capture zone only.
Contain and segregate all stripped material in labelled waste bins; do not allow offcuts or dust to accumulate on adjacent surfaces or escape containment area.
check scraper and tool blades before use for cracks or damage; replace blunt or broken tools immediately to prevent flying fragments or excessive pressure.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start removal until: wet suppression system is operational, dust extractor is running, and respiratory protection is fitted and checked
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression system fails, wet mist is interrupted, or visible dust cloud escapes containment area
🛑 STOP WORK if: unknown material or suspected asbestos is encountered; do not disturb further until licensed assessor confirms material type
🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory protection is removed, damaged, or wearer reports odour breakthrough or breathing difficulty
admin: Secure asbestos removal permit (Class A or B) from SafeWork NSW if ACM identified; file permit on site.
Maintain SDS for all adhesive removal agents on point of use; brief workers on Section 8 (exposure controls) and Section 16 (disposal) before application.
Keep waste register recording all floor coverings, adhesive residue, and ACM removed; classify and dispose according to licensed waste contractor requirements.
Document air monitoring results (if Class A asbestos removal) or dust level checks during stripping; retain records for 5 years.
Conduct toolbox talk before work begins: cover dust hazards, SDS fume warnings, wet suppression requirement, and stop-work triggers.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (ABEK or equivalent, per SDS Section 8) — fitted and tested before use
P2 particulate mask (if wet suppression active and odour not present)
Disposable coveralls (if ACM or vinyl dust risk high)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify wet suppression is active and dust extractor running before each stripping cycle; check visible dust escape at containment boundary.
monitoring.who: Supervisor (site lead or asbestos removal licence holder if ACM present)
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during removal work; check every 30 minutes during extended operations
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of damp floor surface, extractor fan running, no dust haze escaping work area; record check-off on daily site log

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove floor coverings and adhesive
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove floor coverings and adhesive per SWMS

tasks.task: check and clean stripped floor space
tasks.scope: Final visual inspection of demolished area; sweep and remove residual debris; confirm services isolation remains secure; verify no hazardous materials remain
hazards: Residual asbestos fibres or dust inhalation — incomplete removal or re-suspension during final clean
Unidentified hazardous material exposure — concealed contaminants not removed in earlier phases
Trip or fall hazard — debris, protrusions, or uneven floor during final inspection
tasks.dominant_hazard: Residual asbestos fibres or dust inhalation — incomplete removal or re-suspension during final clean
controls: Stop all work immediately if any suspect asbestos material is visible or suspected during inspection.
Visually check floor surface for residual dust, debris, or material fragments before cleaning starts.
Use wet-sweep method only — spray floor lightly with water before sweeping to prevent dust re-suspension.
Collect all swept debris into sealed plastic bags labelled 'Asbestos Waste' — do not shake out or dry-sweep.
Wipe down all exposed surfaces (walls, beams, ducts) with damp cloths — do not dry-brush or use compressed air.
Photograph final cleaned floor space and collect photographic record before handing over area.
Wear Type 5 protective suit, hood, and organic vapour respirator (per SDS) during entire inspection and clean.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any subsequent fit-out works until: project WHS coordinator confirms all asbestos waste has been removed from site to approved facility and disposal docket received
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any suspect asbestos material, friable dust, or non-friable fragments are visible on floor or surfaces after cleaning
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet-sweep method cannot be maintained due to floor drainage or water containment failure
🛑 STOP WORK if: licensed air-monitoring clearance cannot be obtained within project programme window
admin: Confirm air-monitoring consultant (NATA-accredited or equivalent) engaged and available for clearance testing.
Record final inspection date, time, weather conditions, and inspector name in site diary.
Retain photographic record and clearance certificate in project WHS file for minimum 2 years.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (not P2 dust mask) — match to SDS Section 8 requirements for asbestos dust and any residual chemical exposures

monitoring.critical_control: Visually check floor for residual dust or material fragments; photograph before and after cleaning.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during inspection and cleaning; photographic record at start and completion
monitoring.evidence: Dated photographs, site diary entry, clearance certificate from licensed air-monitoring consultant

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: Inspect per specification, photograph defects, report issues

tasks.task: Disconnect electrical, data, and mechanical services
tasks.scope: Licensed electrician to isolate and disconnect all power circuits, data cabling, and mechanical ductwork; mechanical tradesperson to isolate HVAC and plumbing; lock-out switches and confirm isolation before demolition start
hazards: Electric shock or arc flash — contact with live circuits during isolation work
Uncontrolled pressurised mechanical lines — sudden release of HVAC or plumbing pressure
Incomplete or incorrect isolation — residual energy release after lock-out
tasks.dominant_hazard: Electric shock or arc flash — contact with live circuits during isolation work
controls: Obtain single-line diagram or electrical schedule from building owner or facilities manager before isolation work starts.
Licensed electrician to verify all power circuits de-energised at switchboard using multimeter or voltage tester on each circuit before disconnection.
Lock-out each isolated switch or circuit breaker and attach isolation tag with date, time, and licensed electrician name.
Mechanical tradesperson to isolate HVAC pressure lines using ball valves; bleed residual pressure into approved container before disconnection.
Mechanical tradesperson to isolate plumbing water supply at mains valve and drain all lines into approved container before disconnection.
Photograph or video-record each lock-out and isolation point; store record on site for verification.
Prohibit any reconnection or removal of isolation tags except by licensed electrician or mechanical tradesperson who applied them.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start disconnection until: single-line diagram or electrical schedule is obtained and verified on site by licensed electrician.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: multimeter or voltage tester indicates voltage on any circuit after switch isolation or lock-out.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any isolation tag is removed, damaged, or missing from a switch or valve.
🛑 STOP WORK if: residual pressure cannot be fully released from HVAC or plumbing lines before disconnection.
admin: Brief all site personnel on isolation points and lock-out locations before work starts.
tell building owner or facilities manager of isolation commencement and estimated completion time.

monitoring.critical_control: Licensed electrician uses multimeter to verify zero voltage on each circuit immediately before and after lock-out.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during isolation; each circuit verified once before proceeding to next circuit.
monitoring.evidence: Multimeter reading recorded (zero volts) on site log or isolation record; photograph of meter display at each switch.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Disconnect electrical, data, and mechanical
responsibility.WKR: Perform Disconnect electrical, data, and mechanical per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove suspended ceiling system
tasks.scope: Dismantle and remove all suspended ceiling grid, tiles, and associated brackets; collect and sort for waste streams; support head height and prevent falling objects
hazards: Falling ceiling tiles, grid, or brackets — struck on head or body during dismantling
Collapse of unsupported ceiling grid — sudden drop or instability during removal
Entanglement in suspended brackets or wiring — limb or torso trapped during work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Falling ceiling tiles, grid, or brackets — struck on head or body during dismantling
controls: Establish exclusion zone below ceiling work area — minimum 3 m radius, barricade all entry points with shade cloth or hard barriers
Install temporary props or temporary ceiling support at 2 m centres before removing ceiling grid — check prop stability and bearing on floor before work starts
Remove ceiling tiles first by hand into labelled collection bins held at shoulder height — do not throw or drop tiles from height
Dismantle ceiling grid in methodical sections — work from centre outward, support each grid section with temporary props or jack until fully released
Check for and tag asbestos-containing materials found during removal — cease work in that section, isolate area, tell licensed asbestos removal contractor before continuing
Collect all removed material into labelled waste streams — segregate asbestos-suspect material into separate skip for disposal to licensed facility
Wear hard hat, hi-viz shirt or vest, and cut-resistant gloves during dismantling — wear organic vapour respirator if dust or disturbed adhesive dust is visible
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not dismantle grid sections until: temporary props are installed at 2 m centres, verified stable on floor, and no evidence of grid sag or instability is visible
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing material is identified or suspected — isolate section, barricade entry, tell SafeWork NSW and licensed asbestos removal contractor before resuming
🛑 STOP WORK if: ceiling grid shows signs of sag, cracking, or sudden drop during dismantling — move personnel clear, reinforce with additional props, reassess stability before continuing
🛑 STOP WORK if: any exclusion zone barrier is breached or removed — reestablish barricade and brief all site personnel before work resumes
admin: Brief all workers before start: location of exclusion zone, location of temporary props, asbestos identification criteria, stop-work triggers, and location of waste segregation bins
Record all removed material type, location, and destination — document any asbestos-suspect material separately with photos and weight
tell SafeWork NSW if Class A asbestos removal is required — arrange for air monitoring contractor and licensed Class A removal contractor before work recommences
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (P3-rated) — if dust or adhesive vapour is visible; do NOT use P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) for chemical or adhesive dust

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before work start and continuous during ceiling removal
monitoring.evidence: Barricade photo, entry log, worker sign-off at briefing

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove suspended ceiling system
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove suspended ceiling system per SWMS

tasks.task: Collect and stage demolition waste for skip removal
tasks.scope: Consolidate all demolition materials at loading dock; segregate asbestos waste into licensed disposal bins; load skip bins via dock; confirm waste manifests complete before removal
hazards: Asbestos waste cross-contamination — mixing of licensed asbestos bins with general demolition waste
Manual handling injury — strain or back injury during waste consolidation and bin loading
Struck by shifting waste load — unstable pile during stacking or loading via dock
tasks.dominant_hazard: Asbestos waste cross-contamination — mixing of licensed asbestos bins with general demolition waste
controls: Establish separate asbestos waste staging area minimum 3 m from general demolition waste — marked with warning signs and barricade tape.
Load asbestos waste into licensed disposal bins only — verify bin labels match asbestos waste classification (friable or non-friable) before loading.
Prohibit mixing of asbestos and general waste — if cross-contamination occurs, isolate contaminated general waste and treat as asbestos waste per CoP.
Bag all loose asbestos waste in double-thickness plastic bags before placing in licensed bin — seal bags and label with asbestos warning label.
Conduct visual check of each asbestos waste bin contents before sealing — confirm no general demolition material has entered the bin.
Complete waste manifest for asbestos waste showing bin ID, weight, classification, and licensed transporter details before skip removal.
Use mechanical handling (pallet jack or forklift) for loading skip bins via dock — prohibit manual lifting of loads exceeding 20 kg.
Stack waste piles no higher than 1.5 m and make sure stable base — check pile stability before and after loading each additional load.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not load asbestos waste into skip bins until: licensed asbestos bins are on-site, labelled, and segregation area is marked and barricaded.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove skip bins until: waste manifests are completed, signed, and all asbestos bins sealed and verified as containing only asbestos waste.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos waste is found mixed with general demolition waste — isolate contaminated loads and treat all as asbestos waste.
🛑 STOP WORK if: licensed asbestos bins are not available or labelling is incomplete — do not stage asbestos waste without compliant bins.
🛑 STOP WORK if: waste pile becomes unstable or shifts during loading — cease loading and restack to stable configuration.
admin: Confirm SafeWork NSW notification has been lodged and demolition permit issued (if structure >6 m).
Obtain licensed waste transporter details and confirm EPA licence number matches waste manifest.
Record asbestos waste bin ID, weight, classification, and transporter on waste manifest — retain copy for project file.
Provide induction on asbestos waste segregation to all workers before task starts — include no-mix rule and emergency response if spill occurs.
ppe: Disposable coveralls (Type 5) when handling asbestos waste or contaminated materials
P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (or organic vapour mask if asbestos coating dust present) when opening or packing asbestos waste
Safety shoes with ankle support for manual handling and loading

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before sealing each asbestos bin; before each skip removal
monitoring.evidence: Waste manifest signed by supervisor confirming bin contents verified; photograph of sealed bins if required by site protocol

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Collect and stage demolition waste
responsibility.WKR: Perform Collect and stage demolition waste per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove fixed joinery and built-in fittings
tasks.scope: Remove all fixed cupboards, shelving, cabinetry, and door frames; salvage or dispose according to condition; expose prepared surfaces for reinstatement
hazards: Struck by falling joinery or cabinetry during removal — collapse or unplanned drop
Cut or crush injury — fingers or hands in saws, pry bars, or pinch points
Back or strain injury — manual handling of heavy cupboards or long shelving units
tasks.dominant_hazard: Struck by falling joinery or cabinetry during removal — collapse or unplanned drop
controls: Secure all cupboards and shelving to wall frame or temporary props before cutting or prying — prevent collapse during partial removal.
Remove contents and strip internal shelves first — reduce weight and mass before structural removal.
Use two workers minimum for units over 30 kg — manual handling control and spotting for dropped items.
Pry from top corner or central stud only — distribute load and prevent sudden collapse or tip.
Keep hands clear of pinch points and saw path — use pry bar or wedge to open gaps, do not use fingers.
Wear cut-resistant gloves, eye protection, and steel-capped boots — protect against splinters, saw blades, and dropped items.
Establish exclusion zone at least 2 m from removal work — prevent struck-by injury to other workers.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove fixed joinery until: all contents removed, internal shelves stripped, and joinery stability assessed by removing worker.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: suspected asbestos material is encountered (backing board, adhesive, gasket, or pipe wrap) — do not disturb; contact licensed assessor immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: joinery or cupboard shows signs of collapse, tilting, or cracking during cutting or prying — secure immediately and reassess support.
🛑 STOP WORK if: concealed utilities (electrical conduit, water pipe, gas line) are exposed during removal — isolate and confirm safe before proceeding.
admin: If non-friable asbestos identified, tell SafeWork NSW and obtain Class B Removal Licence holder approval before removal.
If friable asbestos suspected, stop work and engage Class A licensed remover — air monitoring and containment required.
tell project manager of asbestos findings and removal method confirmation before work resumes.
make sure all workers hold White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and appropriate asbestos removal competency where applicable.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (if adhesive fumes present during removal) — per SDS Section 8
Dust mask (P2) if dust generation during cutting — wear until dust settles

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before each cupboard or shelving unit removal
monitoring.evidence: Visual check for friable backing, adhesive tape residue, or gasket; photograph if suspected ACM; licensed assessor sign-off if asbestos confirmed

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove fixed joinery and built-in
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove fixed joinery and built-in per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove site establishment and demobilise
tasks.scope: Remove temporary fencing and exclusion signage; remove site equipment and tools; confirm building secured and locked; hand back to owner
hazards: Premature loss of exclusion control — fencing or signage removed before all staff clear site
Public or unauthorised entry — building not fully secured during demobilisation
Trip or manual handling injury — removal of temporary fixtures or equipment
tasks.dominant_hazard: Public or unauthorised entry — building not fully secured during demobilisation
controls: Confirm all hazardous materials removal complete and air clearance certificates obtained before removing any exclusion fencing or signage.
Barricade building entry points with plywood or temporary barriers until final lock-up. Do not remove until building handover confirmed.
Remove temporary fencing in reverse order — perimeter first, then exclusion zones — only after all workers and equipment cleared from site.
Remove signage only after fencing removed and exclusion zone fully delineated. Photograph final site state before removal.
Segregate removed equipment and tools into designated removal zones. Use trolleys or mechanical handling for items over 20 kg.
Brief all site personnel on demob sequence before any exclusion control is removed. Confirm final headcount before gate closure.
Conduct final walkthrough with site supervisor to confirm no tools, debris, or hazardous materials left on site.
Secure all building entry doors and windows with locks verified working. Provide owner with key receipt and sign-off documentation.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove any exclusion fencing or signage until: all hazardous materials removal is complete, air clearance certificates are obtained, and final site walkthrough confirms no active work remains

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not hand building back to owner until: all entry points are secured and locked, keys are handed over with documented receipt, and a final photographic record of secure condition is completed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any unauthorised person enters the exclusion zone during demobilisation or any entry point is found unlocked or unsecured during final checks
🛑 STOP WORK if: hazardous materials survey reports outstanding findings or air clearance cannot be confirmed before exclusion control removal
admin: Obtain written confirmation from site supervisor that all workers have cleared site before removing any temporary fencing.
Obtain air clearance certificates and hazmat removal sign-offs and file with site demob record.
Complete site demobilisation checklist with photographs of secured building and cleared site.
Provide owner with keys, lock verification, and photographic handover documentation.
Record final site condition and sign-off in project close-out documentation.
ppe: High-visibility vest or shirt during final walkthrough and fencing removal
Steel-capped boots during equipment removal and site clearing

monitoring.critical_control: Verify air clearance certificates and confirm all workers off site before removing any exclusion fencing.
monitoring.frequency: Before demobilisation commences and continuously during fencing removal
monitoring.evidence: Signed air clearance certificate, final headcount confirmation, photographic record of cleared site, locked building handover receipt

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

inference.hrcw_category: WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.18 — Asbestos removal work
inference.hrcw_license_class: Asbestos Removal Licence — Class A (friable) or Class B (non-friable)
ppe: Hard hat where overhead risk present
P2 half-face respirator — fit-tested before each shift
Disposable Tyvek coveralls — taped at wrists and ankles
Nitrile gloves — double layer when handling friable material
Decon unit mandatory at zone exit
P2 dust respirator — mandatory during demolition dust generation
Hard hat — mandatory on demolition sites
Arc flash PPE — Class 2 minimum for HV work
Energy-absorbing lanyard — double lanyard where continuous attachment required
P2 respirator — dust and possible asbestos during strip out

CPCCDE3002 — Remove non-friable asbestos (Class B minimum)
Asbestos Assessor accreditation — Class A air monitoring
Demolition Licence — Class B or C (SafeWork NSW)
Electrician Licence — NSW Fair Trading (not SafeWork NSW)
High Voltage Switching authority — where HV work involved

EWP operator licence — WP class where boom exceeds 11m
Traffic Control accreditation — TCP and TCS minimum
Roads Act s.138 consent — before any work in road reserve

Asbestos survey — friable and non-friable asbestos identification before work
Forklift licence — LF class where forklift used for equipment movement
Refrigerant handling licence — ARC licence for refrigerant work
permits: Asbestos removal permit — required before any licensed removal
SafeWork NSW demolition notification — structures over 6m
Pre-demolition hazardous materials survey — by licensed assessor, completed and reviewed before any work
Utility isolation certificates — electricity, gas, water, and telecommunications confirmed disconnected before demolition
Electrical isolation permit — lock-out tag-out before work
Live work permit — where de-energisation not reasonably practicable

Reinstatement bond — lodged with Transport for NSW before work commences

Hazmat survey — completed and reviewed before any demolition commences

Waste management plan — licensed waste contractor engaged before work
Landlord approval — strip out methodology approved before commencing

Crane/hoist permit — where lifting plant to roof or mezzanine

Asbestos Assessor — clearance inspection before re-occupation
Licensed demolition supervisor — on site at all times
Structural engineer sign-off — pre-demolition engineering assessment
Structural monitoring — where adjacent structures at risk, engineer-specified monitoring regime in place before demolition

Verification of isolation — two-person check before commencing
Competent person — pre-use inspection of fall arrest equipment
Rescue plan — documented before work above 2m begins
Rescue equipment — on site and ready for immediate deployment before any elevated work starts
Accredited TCP preparer — Traffic Control Plan prepared by accredited person
Reinstatement standard — must meet AustRoads and TfNSW specifications
Hold point — TfNSW inspection of reinstatement before bond release

Asbestos — asbestos removal by licensed removalist before any other demolition
Waste — segregated waste bins, recycling plan, licensed waste contractor
Existing services — photograph all existing services before removal for as-built record
Structural — do not remove anything structural without engineer approval
Lift plan — for equipment over 500kg or requiring crane/hoist
Spotter — required when moving heavy equipment through occupied areas
Refrigerant leak detection — before and after commissioning
Crane lift plan — if rooftop plant placement required
notifications: SafeWork NSW — 5 business days notice before Class A removal
Utility services disconnection confirmation before start
Energy provider — notification before work on supply authority assets
Transport for NSW — s.138 application minimum 20 business days before
TfNSW network operations — 5 business days before work on state road
Emergency services — notification of road works affecting access routes
Landlord — strip out methodology and program approved in writing before start
Centre management — strip out notification, approved working hours only

Pre-demolition hazardous materials survey mandatory
Structural engineer — signed shoring plan required
WHS Reg 2017 r.291-297 — structural alterations and temporary support obligations
SafeWork NSW Code of Practice: Demolition Work
Pre-demolition survey — must identify ACM, lead paint, PCB, synthetic mineral fibre, and structural hazards
Robotic demolition — where space confined or structural collapse risk elevated; operator remains outside exclusion zone
Progressive demolition — top-down sequence unless engineer specifies otherwise
Overhead powerlines — request de-energisation before demolition plant operates within exclusion zone
Dust suppression — water suppression mandatory during demolition; not optional for urban sites
Waste management — hazardous demolition waste (ACM, lead, PCB) must be segregated and disposed per EPA license requirements
WHS Reg 2017 s.164 — electrical risk management
AS/NZS 3000 — Wiring Rules
Live work — must be last resort, requires specific permit and PPE

WHS Reg 2017 r.305 — rescue procedure required before commencing work at height
Suspension trauma — incapacitated worker must be lowered within 15 minutes; harness straps can cause positional asphyxia
Emergency contacts — on-site personnel trained in rescue procedure before elevated work begins
WHS Reg 2017 r.291-303 — fall prevention hierarchy: (1) eliminate, (2) passive edge protection/guardrail, (3) restraint system, (4) fall arrest, (5) administrative
Edge protection first — guardrails preferred over harness where work area permits fixed barriers
Control line — 2m setback from edge, used only when guardrail not practicable
Exclusion zone required below WAH operations — size proportional to fall/drop zone; physical barrier where practicable, flagging/bunting as minimum
Emergency access must be maintained to all work zones including WAH exclusion zones
Roads Act 1993 (NSW) s.138 — works in road reserve without consent is offence
Classified roads — different approval stream to council local roads

Bond — held until TfNSW satisfied with reinstatement quality
Asbestos — retail fitouts pre-2003 may contain asbestos in vinyl tiles, texture coat, sealants
Services isolation — never assume services are isolated, test before cutting
Waste — fitout waste is C&D waste, licensed facility required for disposal
SafeWork NSW Code of Practice: How to Manage and Control Asbestos in the Workplace
WHS Reg 2017 s.425 — Asbestos register must be maintained
Confirm floor loading capacity along delivery route — not just final position

Refrigerant handling restricted to ARC-licensed technicians
Rooftop plant placement may require crane — separate lift plan and SWMS
Coordinate HVAC commissioning with electrical energisation sequence

task_blocks_raw.task: Confirm site readiness and establish site control
task_blocks_raw.scope: Verify building unoccupied, confirm skip-bin access via loading dock, establish exclusion zones around demolition perimeter, confirm services isolation pre-work checklist complete
hazards: Services still energised — electric shock or arc flash during work setup
Asbestos-containing materials not identified or isolated — inhalation exposure before removal phase
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Services still energised — electric shock or arc flash during work setup
controls: Verify all electrical switchboards are isolated, locked off, and tagged with 'DO NOT OPERATE' notices at point of isolation.
Confirm building is unoccupied — conduct walk-through with site supervisor and record occupancy status in site diary.
Confirm skip-bin access via loading dock is clear — measure and photograph access route before skip placement.
Brief all site personnel on exclusion zone boundaries, services status, and asbestos locations before work starts.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any energised electrical circuit is discovered not listed on isolation checklist or tag-lock is disturbed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: building occupant is found on site or unauthorised person enters exclusion zone.
admin: Record building occupancy confirmation in site diary with date, time, and supervisor name.
Verify all workers hold White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and asbestos-related licences (CPCCDE3002 or CPCCDE3014 as applicable) — check before induction.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

task_blocks_raw.task: Disconnect electrical, data, and mechanical services
task_blocks_raw.scope: Licensed electrician to isolate and disconnect all power circuits, data cabling, and mechanical ductwork; mechanical tradesperson to isolate HVAC and plumbing; lock-out switches and confirm isolation before demolition start
hazards: Electric shock or arc flash — contact with live circuits during isolation work
Uncontrolled pressurised mechanical lines — sudden release of HVAC or plumbing pressure
Incomplete or incorrect isolation — residual energy release after lock-out
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Electric shock or arc flash — contact with live circuits during isolation work
controls: Obtain single-line diagram or electrical schedule from building owner or facilities manager before isolation work starts.
Licensed electrician to verify all power circuits de-energised at switchboard using multimeter or voltage tester on each circuit before disconnection.
Lock-out each isolated switch or circuit breaker and attach isolation tag with date, time, and licensed electrician name.
Mechanical tradesperson to isolate HVAC pressure lines using ball valves; bleed residual pressure into approved container before disconnection.
Mechanical tradesperson to isolate plumbing water supply at mains valve and drain all lines into approved container before disconnection.
Photograph or video-record each lock-out and isolation point; store record on site for verification.
Prohibit any reconnection or removal of isolation tags except by licensed electrician or mechanical tradesperson who applied them.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start disconnection until: single-line diagram or electrical schedule is obtained and verified on site by licensed electrician.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: multimeter or voltage tester indicates voltage on any circuit after switch isolation or lock-out.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any isolation tag is removed, damaged, or missing from a switch or valve.
🛑 STOP WORK if: residual pressure cannot be fully released from HVAC or plumbing lines before disconnection.
admin: Brief all site personnel on isolation points and lock-out locations before work starts.
tell building owner or facilities manager of isolation commencement and estimated completion time.

monitoring.critical_control: Licensed electrician uses multimeter to verify zero voltage on each circuit immediately before and after lock-out.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during isolation; each circuit verified once before proceeding to next circuit.
monitoring.evidence: Multimeter reading recorded (zero volts) on site log or isolation record; photograph of meter display at each switch.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Disconnect electrical, data, and mechanical
responsibility.WKR: Perform Disconnect electrical, data, and mechanical per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class B licence
task_blocks_raw.scope: Licensed asbestos removalist to remove vinyl floor tiles and pipe lagging identified in asbestos survey report; containment, removal, and disposal according to asbestos removal licence and statutory requirements
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.4 — Disturbance of asbestos
hazards: Inhalation of asbestos fibres — exposure during removal, handling, or transport
Contamination of non-removal areas — fibres spread outside containment during work
Inadequate waste containment — asbestos waste exposure during bagging or bin loading
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of asbestos fibres — exposure during removal, handling, or transport
controls: Establish full containment enclosure around removal area — seal doors, windows, penetrations with heavy-duty plastic sheeting and duct tape before any disturbance.
Operate negative pressure unit with HEPA filtration during all removal work — maintain continuous extraction and monitor pressure gauge remains in negative range.
Apply water mist to asbestos materials 15 minutes before removal and keep damp throughout disturbance — use low-pressure spray only, never dry cut or break out.
Place all removed asbestos materials immediately into labelled heavy-duty asbestos waste bags — seal and label each bag with asbestos warning label and licence holder name before any movement.
Decontaminate all waste bags and external containment surfaces with damp cloths before transport from removal area — remove visible dust.
Brief licensed removalist and all workers on removal method, contamination risk zones, and emergency procedures before any work starts.
Monitor air quality during removal using real-time particle counter — record readings every 30 minutes and stop work if airborne fibre level cannot be controlled.
Establish exclusion zone 2 metres beyond containment boundary — prohibit all unauthorised entry and restrict to licensed removalist and safety supervisor only.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start removal until: licensed asbestos removalist and site safety supervisor on site, containment enclosure complete and pressure-tested to negative, water supply confirmed operational, and waste disposal contractor confirmed to receive labelled asbestos waste.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: negative pressure unit fails or containment is breached — seal and do not re-enter until containment is restored and re-tested.
🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression fails or materials become dry during disturbance — re-dampen before continuing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: air monitoring shows fibre level cannot be controlled or respirator fails — evacuate containment, decontaminate, and reassess before re-entry.
admin: tell SafeWork NSW of asbestos removal work according to WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.18 — obtain written acknowledgement.
Complete and retain asbestos removal work method statement including containment design, removal sequence, waste transport route, and disposal contractor details.
Record air monitoring readings on site — retain for 5 years post-removal.
Arrange Class B waste transporter and licensed asbestos waste disposal facility before removal commencement.
Decontaminate site after removal — wipe all non-removal areas and surfaces with damp cloth, dispose of contamination cloths as asbestos waste.
ppe: Type 3 or 4 protective suit with integral hood and booties
Organic vapour and P2 combination respirator (not P2 alone)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: continuous during removal, recorded every 30 minutes
monitoring.evidence: Real-time particle counter readings recorded on site log; negative pressure unit display visible and documented

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove partition walls and structural supports
task_blocks_raw.scope: Strip and remove all non-load-bearing partition walls, studs, and temporary supports; protect primary structure; manage falling-object exclusion zone for full demolition height plus 5m
hazards: Unintended collapse of primary structure — inadequate support or incorrect member identification
Struck by swinging or shifting wall sections — manual or tool-assisted removal
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Falling objects from full demolition height plus 5m exclusion zone — struck by debris or structural member
controls: Install debris containment netting or hoarding to full height plus 2m to capture falling objects and dust within exclusion zone.
Cut and lower wall sections manually or with hand tools; do not drop or swing unsupported sections.
Disconnect or isolate all services within partition walls (electrical, water, gas, HVAC) before removal; tag and verify isolation.
check primary structure for damage, lateral movement, or unintended settlement after each major wall removal; stop work if movement detected.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start partition wall removal until: structural engineer has identified and approved all load-bearing members in writing and confirmed sequence of removal.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: primary structure shows lateral movement, vertical settlement, cracking, or any sign of instability.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached or debris escapes containment netting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unidentified load-bearing member or unexpected structural condition is encountered during removal.
admin: Obtain asbestos removal permit and Class A or B licence before work starts.
Appoint structural engineer to oversee member identification and sequence approval.
Conduct air monitoring during any friable asbestos removal (Class A); record results daily.
ppe: High-visibility vest (all personnel in or near exclusion zone).
Organic vapour respirator or P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) where dust suppression is marginal (SDS Section 8 and site assessment).
Eye protection (impact-rated glasses for cutting and debris removal).

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.who: Structural engineer (approval); Site supervisor (daily verification); Workers (pre-removal briefing).
monitoring.frequency: Structural engineer: before removal sequence approval and after major removal milestones. Supervisor: before each shift and after each large wall removal. Air monitoring: continuous during friable asbestos removal.
monitoring.evidence: Engineer sign-off on member identification drawing; supervisor daily log of exclusion zone integrity and structure condition checks; air monitoring certificates (if Class A); photographic record of containment integrity.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove partition walls and structural
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove partition walls and structural per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.scope: Dismantle and remove all suspended ceiling grid, tiles, and associated brackets; collect and sort for waste streams; support head height and prevent falling objects
hazards: Falling ceiling tiles, grid, or brackets — struck on head or body during dismantling
Collapse of unsupported ceiling grid — sudden drop or instability during removal
Entanglement in suspended brackets or wiring — limb or torso trapped during work
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Falling ceiling tiles, grid, or brackets — struck on head or body during dismantling
controls: Establish exclusion zone below ceiling work area — minimum 3 m radius, barricade all entry points with shade cloth or hard barriers
Install temporary props or temporary ceiling support at 2 m centres before removing ceiling grid — check prop stability and bearing on floor before work starts
Remove ceiling tiles first by hand into labelled collection bins held at shoulder height — do not throw or drop tiles from height
Dismantle ceiling grid in methodical sections — work from centre outward, support each grid section with temporary props or jack until fully released
Check for and tag asbestos-containing materials found during removal — cease work in that section, isolate area, tell licensed asbestos removal contractor before continuing
Collect all removed material into labelled waste streams — segregate asbestos-suspect material into separate skip for disposal to licensed facility
Wear hard hat, hi-viz shirt or vest, and cut-resistant gloves during dismantling — wear organic vapour respirator if dust or disturbed adhesive dust is visible
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not dismantle grid sections until: temporary props are installed at 2 m centres, verified stable on floor, and no evidence of grid sag or instability is visible
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing material is identified or suspected — isolate section, barricade entry, tell SafeWork NSW and licensed asbestos removal contractor before resuming
🛑 STOP WORK if: ceiling grid shows signs of sag, cracking, or sudden drop during dismantling — move personnel clear, reinforce with additional props, reassess stability before continuing
🛑 STOP WORK if: any exclusion zone barrier is breached or removed — reestablish barricade and brief all site personnel before work resumes
admin: Brief all workers before start: location of exclusion zone, location of temporary props, asbestos identification criteria, stop-work triggers, and location of waste segregation bins
Record all removed material type, location, and destination — document any asbestos-suspect material separately with photos and weight
tell SafeWork NSW if Class A asbestos removal is required — arrange for air monitoring contractor and licensed Class A removal contractor before work recommences
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (P3-rated) — if dust or adhesive vapour is visible; do NOT use P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) for chemical or adhesive dust

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before work start and continuous during ceiling removal
monitoring.evidence: Barricade photo, entry log, worker sign-off at briefing

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove suspended ceiling system
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove suspended ceiling system per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove floor coverings and adhesive backing
task_blocks_raw.scope: Strip vinyl tiles, carpet, and adhesive remnants from concrete floor slab; include perimeter skirting and trims; contain dust and manage waste for appropriate disposal
hazards: Dust inhalation — silica or vinyl dust released during stripping and adhesive removal
Chemical exposure — adhesive fumes or solvents during wet removal or grinding
Cut or puncture wound — sharp tools or concealed fasteners during stripping work
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Dust inhalation — silica or vinyl dust released during stripping and adhesive removal
controls: Establish wet suppression protocol: spray floor with water mist before and during scraping to prevent dust release; maintain damp surface throughout stripping work.
Install local exhaust ventilation or portable dust extractor with HEPA filter at point of removal; maintain continuous extraction during scraping and grinding operations.
Wear organic vapour respirator (per SDS Section 8) when adhesive fumes present; switch to P2 particulate mask if only dust generation observed and wet suppression fails.
Barricade work area with plastic sheeting and tape seams; restrict access to licensed floor stripping personnel only; maintain negative air pressure if available.
Check floor substrate before stripping for concealed fasteners, wire mesh, or unknown materials; stop work immediately if asbestos-containing material is suspected.
Use hand tools (floor scraper, putty knife) in preference to power grinders where practicable; if grinding required, operate within dust extraction capture zone only.
Contain and segregate all stripped material in labelled waste bins; do not allow offcuts or dust to accumulate on adjacent surfaces or escape containment area.
check scraper and tool blades before use for cracks or damage; replace blunt or broken tools immediately to prevent flying fragments or excessive pressure.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start removal until: wet suppression system is operational, dust extractor is running, and respiratory protection is fitted and checked
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression system fails, wet mist is interrupted, or visible dust cloud escapes containment area
🛑 STOP WORK if: unknown material or suspected asbestos is encountered; do not disturb further until licensed assessor confirms material type
🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory protection is removed, damaged, or wearer reports odour breakthrough or breathing difficulty
admin: Secure asbestos removal permit (Class A or B) from SafeWork NSW if ACM identified; file permit on site.
Maintain SDS for all adhesive removal agents on point of use; brief workers on Section 8 (exposure controls) and Section 16 (disposal) before application.
Keep waste register recording all floor coverings, adhesive residue, and ACM removed; classify and dispose according to licensed waste contractor requirements.
Document air monitoring results (if Class A asbestos removal) or dust level checks during stripping; retain records for 5 years.
Conduct toolbox talk before work begins: cover dust hazards, SDS fume warnings, wet suppression requirement, and stop-work triggers.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (ABEK or equivalent, per SDS Section 8) — fitted and tested before use
P2 particulate mask (if wet suppression active and odour not present)
Disposable coveralls (if ACM or vinyl dust risk high)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify wet suppression is active and dust extractor running before each stripping cycle; check visible dust escape at containment boundary.
monitoring.who: Supervisor (site lead or asbestos removal licence holder if ACM present)
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during removal work; check every 30 minutes during extended operations
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of damp floor surface, extractor fan running, no dust haze escaping work area; record check-off on daily site log

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove floor coverings and adhesive
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove floor coverings and adhesive per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove fixed joinery and built-in fittings
task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove all fixed cupboards, shelving, cabinetry, and door frames; salvage or dispose according to condition; expose prepared surfaces for reinstatement
hazards: Struck by falling joinery or cabinetry during removal — collapse or unplanned drop
Cut or crush injury — fingers or hands in saws, pry bars, or pinch points
Back or strain injury — manual handling of heavy cupboards or long shelving units
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Struck by falling joinery or cabinetry during removal — collapse or unplanned drop
controls: Secure all cupboards and shelving to wall frame or temporary props before cutting or prying — prevent collapse during partial removal.
Remove contents and strip internal shelves first — reduce weight and mass before structural removal.
Use two workers minimum for units over 30 kg — manual handling control and spotting for dropped items.
Pry from top corner or central stud only — distribute load and prevent sudden collapse or tip.
Keep hands clear of pinch points and saw path — use pry bar or wedge to open gaps, do not use fingers.
Wear cut-resistant gloves, eye protection, and steel-capped boots — protect against splinters, saw blades, and dropped items.
Establish exclusion zone at least 2 m from removal work — prevent struck-by injury to other workers.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove fixed joinery until: all contents removed, internal shelves stripped, and joinery stability assessed by removing worker.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: suspected asbestos material is encountered (backing board, adhesive, gasket, or pipe wrap) — do not disturb; contact licensed assessor immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: joinery or cupboard shows signs of collapse, tilting, or cracking during cutting or prying — secure immediately and reassess support.
🛑 STOP WORK if: concealed utilities (electrical conduit, water pipe, gas line) are exposed during removal — isolate and confirm safe before proceeding.
admin: If non-friable asbestos identified, tell SafeWork NSW and obtain Class B Removal Licence holder approval before removal.
If friable asbestos suspected, stop work and engage Class A licensed remover — air monitoring and containment required.
tell project manager of asbestos findings and removal method confirmation before work resumes.
make sure all workers hold White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and appropriate asbestos removal competency where applicable.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (if adhesive fumes present during removal) — per SDS Section 8
Dust mask (P2) if dust generation during cutting — wear until dust settles

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before each cupboard or shelving unit removal
monitoring.evidence: Visual check for friable backing, adhesive tape residue, or gasket; photograph if suspected ACM; licensed assessor sign-off if asbestos confirmed

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove fixed joinery and built-in
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove fixed joinery and built-in per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Collect and stage demolition waste for skip removal
task_blocks_raw.scope: Consolidate all demolition materials at loading dock; segregate asbestos waste into licensed disposal bins; load skip bins via dock; confirm waste manifests complete before removal
hazards: Asbestos waste cross-contamination — mixing of licensed asbestos bins with general demolition waste
Manual handling injury — strain or back injury during waste consolidation and bin loading
Struck by shifting waste load — unstable pile during stacking or loading via dock
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Asbestos waste cross-contamination — mixing of licensed asbestos bins with general demolition waste
controls: Establish separate asbestos waste staging area minimum 3 m from general demolition waste — marked with warning signs and barricade tape.
Load asbestos waste into licensed disposal bins only — verify bin labels match asbestos waste classification (friable or non-friable) before loading.
Prohibit mixing of asbestos and general waste — if cross-contamination occurs, isolate contaminated general waste and treat as asbestos waste per CoP.
Bag all loose asbestos waste in double-thickness plastic bags before placing in licensed bin — seal bags and label with asbestos warning label.
Conduct visual check of each asbestos waste bin contents before sealing — confirm no general demolition material has entered the bin.
Complete waste manifest for asbestos waste showing bin ID, weight, classification, and licensed transporter details before skip removal.
Use mechanical handling (pallet jack or forklift) for loading skip bins via dock — prohibit manual lifting of loads exceeding 20 kg.
Stack waste piles no higher than 1.5 m and make sure stable base — check pile stability before and after loading each additional load.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not load asbestos waste into skip bins until: licensed asbestos bins are on-site, labelled, and segregation area is marked and barricaded.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove skip bins until: waste manifests are completed, signed, and all asbestos bins sealed and verified as containing only asbestos waste.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos waste is found mixed with general demolition waste — isolate contaminated loads and treat all as asbestos waste.
🛑 STOP WORK if: licensed asbestos bins are not available or labelling is incomplete — do not stage asbestos waste without compliant bins.
🛑 STOP WORK if: waste pile becomes unstable or shifts during loading — cease loading and restack to stable configuration.
admin: Confirm SafeWork NSW notification has been lodged and demolition permit issued (if structure >6 m).
Obtain licensed waste transporter details and confirm EPA licence number matches waste manifest.
Record asbestos waste bin ID, weight, classification, and transporter on waste manifest — retain copy for project file.
Provide induction on asbestos waste segregation to all workers before task starts — include no-mix rule and emergency response if spill occurs.
ppe: Disposable coveralls (Type 5) when handling asbestos waste or contaminated materials
P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (or organic vapour mask if asbestos coating dust present) when opening or packing asbestos waste
Safety shoes with ankle support for manual handling and loading

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before sealing each asbestos bin; before each skip removal
monitoring.evidence: Waste manifest signed by supervisor confirming bin contents verified; photograph of sealed bins if required by site protocol

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Collect and stage demolition waste
responsibility.WKR: Perform Collect and stage demolition waste per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: check and clean stripped floor space
task_blocks_raw.scope: Final visual inspection of demolished area; sweep and remove residual debris; confirm services isolation remains secure; verify no hazardous materials remain
hazards: Residual asbestos fibres or dust inhalation — incomplete removal or re-suspension during final clean
Unidentified hazardous material exposure — concealed contaminants not removed in earlier phases
Trip or fall hazard — debris, protrusions, or uneven floor during final inspection
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Residual asbestos fibres or dust inhalation — incomplete removal or re-suspension during final clean
controls: Stop all work immediately if any suspect asbestos material is visible or suspected during inspection.
Visually check floor surface for residual dust, debris, or material fragments before cleaning starts.
Use wet-sweep method only — spray floor lightly with water before sweeping to prevent dust re-suspension.
Collect all swept debris into sealed plastic bags labelled 'Asbestos Waste' — do not shake out or dry-sweep.
Wipe down all exposed surfaces (walls, beams, ducts) with damp cloths — do not dry-brush or use compressed air.
Photograph final cleaned floor space and collect photographic record before handing over area.
Wear Type 5 protective suit, hood, and organic vapour respirator (per SDS) during entire inspection and clean.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any subsequent fit-out works until: project WHS coordinator confirms all asbestos waste has been removed from site to approved facility and disposal docket received
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any suspect asbestos material, friable dust, or non-friable fragments are visible on floor or surfaces after cleaning
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet-sweep method cannot be maintained due to floor drainage or water containment failure
🛑 STOP WORK if: licensed air-monitoring clearance cannot be obtained within project programme window
admin: Confirm air-monitoring consultant (NATA-accredited or equivalent) engaged and available for clearance testing.
Record final inspection date, time, weather conditions, and inspector name in site diary.
Retain photographic record and clearance certificate in project WHS file for minimum 2 years.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (not P2 dust mask) — match to SDS Section 8 requirements for asbestos dust and any residual chemical exposures

monitoring.critical_control: Visually check floor for residual dust or material fragments; photograph before and after cleaning.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during inspection and cleaning; photographic record at start and completion
monitoring.evidence: Dated photographs, site diary entry, clearance certificate from licensed air-monitoring consultant

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: Inspect per specification, photograph defects, report issues

task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove temporary fencing and exclusion signage; remove site equipment and tools; confirm building secured and locked; hand back to owner
hazards: Premature loss of exclusion control — fencing or signage removed before all staff clear site
Public or unauthorised entry — building not fully secured during demobilisation
Trip or manual handling injury — removal of temporary fixtures or equipment
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Public or unauthorised entry — building not fully secured during demobilisation
controls: Confirm all hazardous materials removal complete and air clearance certificates obtained before removing any exclusion fencing or signage.
Barricade building entry points with plywood or temporary barriers until final lock-up. Do not remove until building handover confirmed.
Remove temporary fencing in reverse order — perimeter first, then exclusion zones — only after all workers and equipment cleared from site.
Remove signage only after fencing removed and exclusion zone fully delineated. Photograph final site state before removal.
Segregate removed equipment and tools into designated removal zones. Use trolleys or mechanical handling for items over 20 kg.
Brief all site personnel on demob sequence before any exclusion control is removed. Confirm final headcount before gate closure.
Conduct final walkthrough with site supervisor to confirm no tools, debris, or hazardous materials left on site.
Secure all building entry doors and windows with locks verified working. Provide owner with key receipt and sign-off documentation.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove any exclusion fencing or signage until: all hazardous materials removal is complete, air clearance certificates are obtained, and final site walkthrough confirms no active work remains

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not hand building back to owner until: all entry points are secured and locked, keys are handed over with documented receipt, and a final photographic record of secure condition is completed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any unauthorised person enters the exclusion zone during demobilisation or any entry point is found unlocked or unsecured during final checks
🛑 STOP WORK if: hazardous materials survey reports outstanding findings or air clearance cannot be confirmed before exclusion control removal
admin: Obtain written confirmation from site supervisor that all workers have cleared site before removing any temporary fencing.
Obtain air clearance certificates and hazmat removal sign-offs and file with site demob record.
Complete site demobilisation checklist with photographs of secured building and cleared site.
Provide owner with keys, lock verification, and photographic handover documentation.
Record final site condition and sign-off in project close-out documentation.
ppe: High-visibility vest or shirt during final walkthrough and fencing removal
Steel-capped boots during equipment removal and site clearing

monitoring.critical_control: Verify air clearance certificates and confirm all workers off site before removing any exclusion fencing.
monitoring.frequency: Before demobilisation commences and continuously during fencing removal
monitoring.evidence: Signed air clearance certificate, final headcount confirmation, photographic record of cleared site, locked building handover receipt

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues
